DoomwatchConnections

Privacy Policy

Updated 27 November 2026

What stays in your browser

Doomwatch uses browser storage for your display name, hero, watched titles, custom entries, music and spoiler preferences, and cookie notice choice. You can clear these by removing Doomwatch’s site data in your browser. This also removes your saved progress on that browser.

What goes on the signature wall

When you sign, Doomwatch sends your display name and hero to the wall service. Everyone who visits the wall can see those details and the Earth number and signing order assigned by the site. Use a nickname you’re comfortable making public. The wall displays up to 100 signatures. Older entries rotate out as new ones are added.

Wall cookie and signing history

Doomwatch uses a wall cookie with a randomly generated identifier to remember whether this browser has signed and which position it received. The cookie lasts up to 400 days unless you clear it sooner. The wall service keeps an identifier and signing order after the public entry rotates out to enforce the one-signature rule. Clearing browser data does not remove an entry from the public wall or erase the server-side record.

Share links and downloads

A readiness link you create can include your display name, hero, and progress. Anyone you give the link to can view those details. The same information may be visible in a cover you save and share.

Hosting, fonts, and external sites

Netlify serves the main site, and the connected Sites backend runs the shared wall. Hosting services may process ordinary connection information such as your IP address and browser details to deliver and operate the site. The Watchlist and Connections pages also request typefaces from Google Fonts. Streaming guides, ticket sellers, and social profiles apply their own privacy practices when you visit them. See Netlify’s Privacy Statement and the Google Fonts privacy FAQ.

Privacy requests

Contact Ash X Vend on X with questions about your information or a request to remove a wall entry. Use a private message where available and identify the entry by its display name and Earth number.
